original_question: Is the gene associated with Roberts syndrome located at 6q21.1 on chromosome 6?

final_qi.question: Is the gene associated with Roberts syndrome located at 6q21.1 on chromosome 6?
final_qi.long_answer: Roberts syndrome (also known as SC phocomelia) is caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the ESCO2 gene (Establishment of Sister Chromatid Cohesion N-acetyltransferase 2). The ESCO2 locus is situated on the short arm of chromosome 8, cytogenetic band 8p21.1. It is not located on chromosome 6, and there is no established linkage of Roberts syndrome to the 6q21.1 region. Therefore, the statement that the gene associated with Roberts syndrome is located at 6q21.1 on chromosome 6 is incorrect.
